newsitem.title: UK: ISDA opposes any ECB move for derivatives reserves.
newsitem.headline: ISDA opposes any ECB move for derivatives reserves.

text.p: The International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) said on Thursday it was concerned about the possibility the European Central Bank (ECB) might impose reserve requirements on derivatives.

The possibility was set out in a January document from the European Monetary Institute (EMI), forerunner to the ECB, entitled, "The Single Monetary Policy in Stage Three: Specification of the Operational Framework."
The ECB will be established once European monetary union comes into force.
The document proposed a European Community (EU) regulation empowering the ECB to impose reserves on off-balance sheet instruments, including derivatives.

"The EMI proposals raise a spectre over a major financial market used by governments, financial institutions and companies throughout the EU to manage their financial risks," said Gay Evans, ISDA chairman and senior managing director of Bankers Trust International.
"Our analysis shows that imposing reserves on derivatives would drive up costs, forcing markets offshore, even with reserves set at a low level and partly remunerated."

Evans said there would be a host of practical and technical difficulties in imposing such reserves, largely because derivatives would rarely have any effect on the creation of the single currency's liquidity and only a marginal effect in those rare cases.
